page: Hetzner Cloud cx23 is an entry-level virtual server based on the x86_64 architecture, utilizing QEMU virtualization. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon cores running at 2.0 GHz with a shared CPU allocation model. The system is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 1.95 GB of RAM per core. Local storage consists of a 40 GB SSD, and the instance does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data places the cx23 in the lower performance tiers. In stress-ng testing, both single-core (1028.88) and multi-core (2016.78) CPU performance fall within the bottom 10% of tested servers. Memory bandwidth benchmarks show a read-only small block speed of 149.36 GB/sec and a large block write speed of 16.93 GB/sec, which is categorized in the bottom 25%. Geekbench scores reflect similar trends, with a single-core score of 713.0 and a multi-core score of 1222.0.

Due to the shared CPU allocation and lower-tier benchmark results, this server presents a clear tradeoff between raw performance and cost efficiency. It is designed for low-intensity workloads where resource density and budget are prioritized over high-throughput processing. Suitable applications include basic web serving, lightweight background tasks, small-scale development environments, and simple utility services that do not require sustained high CPU utilization.
